exact_based_clause: More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.
exact_no_hidden_multiplicity_clause:
The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

axiom_checks.local_proof: Factor Proof1.1 verifies matched weights. Proof4.1 has S^2=0 and algebraic finite columns, so C and C^-1 give an actual algebraic field basis.
Factor Proof2.1/3.1 establish modular divided E/F and toral intertwining; Proof4.1 divides the cross terms by the adjacent distinct primes p,h and proves actual integral stability.
Factor Proof5.1 uses the standard compatible bar and bar-fixed shear coefficients; C commutes with that bar, hence it fixes every raw basis vector.

axiom_checks.axiom: crystal local chart and residue basis
axiom_checks.local_proof: Factor Proof1.1 gives 1/p,1/h in q A_0, with bar-dual infinity behavior. Proof5.1 shows C and C^-1 preserve the standard direct-sum charts and are identity on residues; finite string Kashiwara shifts therefore preserve the raw chart and give the residue crystal.

integrability: Each algebraic vector has finitely many standard finite divided-string constituents; a finite maximum of their nilpotence bounds annihilates it in both E and F directions. The homogeneous shear is only a basis change.
weight_multiplicity: M_0 contains one independent standard middle vector from every constituent (all n_j are even), so is countably infinite dimensional. No finite weight dimension is an axiom of either exact local definition. The example is deliberately outside bounded finite-weight-space O_int.
balanced_boundary: The CEX states the natural unrestricted integral reduction map explicitly. It does not refute or alter the finite-dimensional contract of def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map.

crystal_definition.clause_check: Definition(i)-(vi) require free field-spanning graded charts, free weight pieces, shift stability, a graded residue basis and partial inverse shifts. They impose no finite rank. Its dimension/rank/cardinality equation is valid also for infinite cardinalities. The periodic standard divided direct-sum chart has these six properties coefficientwise, and C is a chart automorphism with identity residue.

string_supplier_no_multiplicity_bound.quote: Coefficients beyond a string's bottom are specified to be zero; arbitrary killed coefficients at the top are not allowed. No finite-dimensionality of $M$ or of its weight spaces, no bounded support, no uniform nilpotence and no choice principle is assumed; $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the integer pairing of the datum ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]) and $F_i^{(n)}$ is the divided power of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].
